\subsection*{1.\quad $h_0$ is gauge-phobic exactly, and the $VV$ couplings obey a sum rule}
\emph{derived here} --- \S2\par\medskip
\textbf{Claim}\par\nopagebreak
\begin{equation*}\small g_{h_iVV} = g^{\rm SM}\,(R_S^{\mathsf T}\hat n)_i = g^{\rm SM}(\cos\delta,\,0,\,\sin\delta),\qquad \sum_i g_{h_iVV}^2 = (g^{\rm SM})^2 \end{equation*}
\textbf{Result}\par\nopagebreak
\begin{equation*}\small {R_S^{\mathsf T}\hat n} = \left[\begin{matrix}\cos{\left(\delta \right)} & 0 & \sin{\left(\delta \right)}\end{matrix}\right] \end{equation*}
\textbf{Independent checks}\begin{itemize}\itemsep0pt
\item $R_A$'s first column verified to be the unit vacuum direction
\item the SM reference read off the $\delta\to0$ limit, not typed in
\item $W$ and $Z$ couplings both equal $g^{\rm SM}\times$ the same projection
\item the zero survives a generic vacuum angle $\varphi_v$, so it is orthogonality and not the $\sqrt3$ alignment
\end{itemize}
\textbf{Would be falsified by:} a non-zero middle projection at generic $\varphi_v$, or a $\delta\to0$ reference differing from $i g_w m_W$\par
